drhp.business: DML operates two primary business lines: the manufacture and supply of soft ferrite magnets to automobile OEMs, railway projects, electronic component manufacturers and aerospace OEMs in India and worldwide through its soft ferrite magnet division, and the design, manufacture and supply of garment trims (woven labels, heat transfers, fabric printed labels, elastic and non-elastic tapes) primarily to major garment and textile companies in India. The company closed its Hard Ferrite Magnet Division during the year due to sustained financial underperformance and structural market challenges.
drhp.end_markets: automobile OEMs|railway projects|electronic component manufacturers|aerospace OEMs|garment and textile companies in India|worldwide (magnet exports)
drhp.expansion: The Company achieved full utilisation of its installed production capacity at the Tirupur, Tamil Nadu trims facility in its first full year of operation and is evaluating planned capacity expansion there in the coming year, with increased infrastructure and facilities to allow scalability and ramp-up of incremental machinery and manpower. The soft ferrite magnet division's joint venture with PREMO S.L., Spain progressed during the year, enabling fuller utilisation of the division's capacity and expanding participation in higher value-added applications; approximately 20% of the targeted JV business has been secured and validation completed for nearly nine additional parts. The Hard Ferrite Magnet Division (Ambad, Nashik) was closed on 30th January 2026 due to sustained financial underperformance, structural market challenges, low capacity utilisation and high capital intensity.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Delta Manufacturing Limited (DML), incorporated in 1982, manufactures soft ferrite magnets for automobile, railway, electronics and aerospace OEMs and garment trims for Indian textile and garment companies.

business_model.title: Business (RHP)
business_model.body: DML operates two primary business lines: the manufacture and supply of soft ferrite magnets to automobile OEMs, railway projects, electronic component manufacturers and aerospace OEMs in India and worldwide through its soft ferrite magnet division, and the design, manufacture and supply of garment trims (woven labels, heat transfers, fabric printed labels, elastic and non-elastic tapes) primarily to major garment and textile companies in India. The company closed its Hard Ferrite Magnet Division during the year due to sustained financial underperformance and structural market challenges.

group_structure.title: Related (RHP)
group_structure.body:
- **DML Ferrites Private Limited** Wholly-owned (100%) subsidiary, effective 08th November 2024.
- **Rhine Estates Limited** Was a subsidiary up to 04th October 2024.
- **MMG Ferrites Private Limited** Joint venture company (50% holding) w.e.f. 24th March 2025; engaged in soft ferrite magnet manufacture; was previously a subsidiary from 2nd May 2024 to 23rd March 2025.
- **AZB & Partners** Enterprise over which KMPs/relatives exercise significant influence; provided professional/legal services to the Company.
- **Myra Mall Management Company Private Limited** Enterprise over which KMPs/relatives exercise significant influence; counterparty for loans and interest transactions with the Company.
- **Delta Corp Limited** Enterprise over which KMPs/relatives exercise significant influence; counterparty for rent/reimbursement and purchase of goods/services transactions.

- automobile OEMs
- railway projects
- electronic component manufacturers
- aerospace OEMs
- garment and textile companies in India
- worldwide (magnet exports)

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Record automobile volumes, rising EV penetration and the Government's push to build a domestic electronics component ecosystem are structural tailwinds for the ferrite magnet division.
- FTAs with key markets (UK, EU, Oman, New Zealand) and the shift towards branded apparel support medium-term demand for garment trims.
- Broad-based revival in private consumption, aided by GST 2.0, income tax relief and lower interest rates, bodes well for sustained demand in the automotive, electronics and textile/apparel segments the company operates in.
- Elevated US tariffs created uncertainty for export-oriented garment customers during most of the year.
- The India automotive industry delivered record FY26 volumes across every vehicle category, a demand backdrop relevant to the magnet division's OEM customers.
- Joint venture with PREMO S.L. has secured approximately 20% of the targeted business and completed validation for nearly nine additional parts, providing a pipeline expected to significantly increase business volumes in the coming year.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company achieved full utilisation of its installed production capacity at the Tirupur, Tamil Nadu trims facility in its first full year of operation and is evaluating planned capacity expansion there in the coming year, with increased infrastructure and facilities to allow scalability and ramp-up of incremental machinery and manpower. The soft ferrite magnet division's joint venture with PREMO S.L., Spain progressed during the year, enabling fuller utilisation of the division's capacity and expanding participation in higher value-added applications; approximately 20% of the targeted JV business has been secured and validation completed for nearly nine additional parts. The Hard Ferrite Magnet Division (Ambad, Nashik) was closed on 30th January 2026 due to sustained financial underperformance, structural market challenges, low capacity utilisation and high capital intensity.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body: technology: joint venture with PREMO S.L., Spain gives the magnet division access to technology and higher value-added soft ferrite products — evidence: validation completed for nearly nine additional parts and approximately 20% of the targeted JV business secured

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The company depends on imported raw material for soft ferrites, exposing it to import cost and currency risk.
- Delayed payments and inconsistent honouring of purchase terms by certain clients strain working capital management.
- Elevated US tariffs affected export-linked demand for most of the year, and the conflict in West Asia posed risks to supply chains, commodity prices and freight costs towards year-end.
- The commodity nature of the product limits the Company's ability to command pricing power.
- Supply to OEMs provides volume stability but creates a time lag between input cost inflation and the ability to pass on higher costs.
- Flagged as a threat to the magnet segment given intense price competition from Chinese suppliers.
- Elevated US tariffs during most of the year created volatility in export demand from the Company's garment customers, affecting the trims segment.
- The trims segment faces competition from unorganised players, a structural challenge to pricing and market share.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue transitioning from traditional products to a wider range of technologically advanced components and sub-systems, integrating new strategic businesses with the existing business.
- Build capability by establishing new locations for manufacturing and R&D, pursuing select value-accretive partnerships and expanding the customer base.
- Evaluate capacity expansion in the trims segment through increased infrastructure and facilities to allow scalability and ramp-up of incremental machinery and manpower.
- Participate in higher value-added soft ferrite magnet applications, including those linked to electric mobility and electronics, through the PREMO S.L. joint venture.
- Restructure the customer and product portfolio with the objective of growing the business profitably.
